* you · 1
Using the CURRENT saved Atlas notebook only, explain in under 250 words why ArtCraft need not win commercially for software rents to reprice; distinguish fast multiple compression from slow paid migration, and explain how the prior February software selloff changes the information-asymmetry thesis. Cite E14 or E15 and propose one discriminating public observation.
* model · 2
**Fact:** E14 reports a broad software selloff on 2026-02-04 as investors reassessed application-layer disruption after an Anthropic tool release. E15 shows the Design & Creative Tools median forward P/E fell from 24.2 at start-2026 to 15.4 by 2026-09-28 — a sector bucket, not Adobe’s multiple.

**Inference:** Software rents can reprice through fast multiple compression before slow paid migration. Faster clock: investors shorten expected subscription duration/terminal growth. Slower clock: renewals, realized pricing, migration and margins validate durability later. ArtCraft need not win commercially because the mechanism is contestable software rents and replication breadth, not ArtCraft revenue.

**Assumption:** Markets price expected durability, and a sector bucket is a usable prior-pessimism control.

**How February changes the asymmetry thesis:** The broad AI-software threat is already public, so a hidden sector-wide story is untenable. The edge must be incremental surprise — replication cost, breadth or familiar-workflow preservation that existing expectations underweight — not mere AI disruption.

**One discriminating public observation:** A pre-registered, timestamped independent benchmark measuring build cost/time and task/file/plug-in/team fidelity across multiple open creative reimplementations versus Adobe and free controls, alongside Adobe-specific forward estimate revisions versus peers. That would show whether ArtCraft adds unpriced information or repeats already-priced pessimism.

No trade recommendation.

* say ▸  (RET to message the task, C-Enter to steer it)
